reviewers.summary: The report path loses all package changes when the staged inventory is empty. This also prevents the named 150-package batching case from producing its expected requests.

findingList.message: An empty staged snapshot causes awk to treat every after-snapshot row as a before entry, so newly installed packages are omitted.

evidence.codePathTraced: report_packages passes the staged snapshot and after snapshot to awk; the first-file check uses NR==FNR.
evidence.failureScenario: When the staged snapshot is empty and the after snapshot contains 150 packages, NR equals FNR for every after-snapshot row, so awk treats them all as baseline entries and emits no updates. The report sends no batches, losing the installs.

reviewers.summary: The empty-baseline path drops all package changes, including the explicit 150-package batching case. The new shell tests also are not invoked by the repository’s configured test command or workflows.

findingList.message: An empty staged listing causes report to treat every after entry as preexisting, dropping installed packages instead of reporting them.

evidence.codePathTraced: report_packages passes the staged and after files to awk, whose NR==FNR branch distinguishes the first file from the second.
evidence.failureScenario: If stage succeeds with an empty package listing, NR==FNR remains true while awk reads the after file. Its packages are treated as baseline entries, so report emits no updates; the 150-package case in test_report_request_shape_and_chunks would send no requests.

findingList.message: The acceptance-criteria tests are not wired into the repository’s test command, so CI does not run them.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test file invokes its three cases only through its final shell loop. The repository’s frontend test script runs node --test tests/*.test.mjs, and the available workflows contain no invocation of this shell script.
evidence.failureScenario: A PR can leave test_stage_then_report_sends_differences, test_report_request_shape_and_chunks, and test_hook_fail_safe failing or broken while the configured test command never executes them.

reviewers.summary: The hook can expose the configured API key to network observers because it accepts HTTP API URLs and sends the key over that connection.

findingList.message: A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures: the hook sends X-API-Key over plaintext HTTP when configured with an HTTP URL. Require HTTPS when sending the key, or otherwise prevent the credential from being transmitted without TLS.

evidence.codePathTraced: The configured API URL is passed directly to curl, and the configured API key is sent in the X-API-Key header without requiring HTTPS.
evidence.failureScenario: With the HTTP API URL used in the acceptance test, a network observer can read the request and capture the API key, then use it to authenticate to the ingest API.
